title: Parallel Complex Diffusion for Scalable Time Series Generation

problem.claim: Time-series diffusion models must recover highly entangled cross-time relationships, making generative modeling difficult.

gap.claim: Existing frequency-aware methods mainly use the DFT for estimator blocks within temporal DDPM/SDE frameworks, while frequency-native diffusion paths face a barrier from complex-valued dynamics.

contributions.claim: PaCoDi constructs a frequency-native diffusion path in the spectral domain using parallel real-valued estimators for real and imaginary components.

The work establishes statistical orthogonality of spectral Gaussian noise, quadrature forward transitions, conditional reverse factorization, and a continuous-time extension through a Spectral Wiener Process.
The method adds a Mean Field Theory approximation with an Interactive Correction Branch and uses Hermitian symmetry to reduce attention FLOPs without information loss.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior generative quality and computational efficiency against five state-of-the-art baselines across five benchmarks for unconditional and conditional generation.
The authors report that Hermitian symmetry reduces attention FLOPs by 50% without information loss.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion-model difficulty is tied to data dependency structure, and temporal dependence creates highly entangled relationships in time series.
The DFT is used to transform temporal dependencies into spectral modes and better align the data manifold with diffusion noise and dynamics.
Prior frequency-aware approaches do not resolve the mathematical barrier to frequency-native diffusion with complex-valued dynamics.
PaCoDi uses parallel real-valued estimators in the spectral domain and provides discrete and continuous-time theoretical constructions.
The framework adds marginal-coupling correction and computational reduction mechanisms, followed by experiments on five benchmarks against five baselines.

source_observation.claim: The method changes the diffusion-space topology by representing temporal dependencies as spectral modes.

interpretation.claim: Changing the representation in which the generative process operates may reduce the burden of modeling structured dependencies.

application.claim: For other structured sequential data, evaluate whether a domain-specific transform can simplify dependency structure before designing the generative dynamics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that spectral representations are beneficial for all time-series distributions or tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the five benchmarks or five baselines.
Quantitative quality and efficiency results are not provided.
The abstract does not describe data characteristics, hyperparameters, or ablation results.
